state.claim: More than 225,000 people dead, 225,000. The estimates are, if we’d have acted responsibly, there’d be 160,000 fewer dead than there are today, because of covid-19.
state.query: What primary data source (e.g., CDC, state health departments, Johns Hopkins) supports a covid-19 death count exceeding 225,000 at the time of the statement?

candidates.title: Surveillance and Data Analytics | Covid | CDC
candidates.snippet: This page provides an overview of COVID-19 data and trends over time. Other COVID-19 related data visualizations (previously on CDC’s COVID Data Tracker) are provided in the resources section at the bottom of this page.

candidates.title: COVID-19 Data from the National Center for Health Statistics
candidates.snippet: Deaths Access provisional death counts based on information obtained from death certificates.

candidates.title: FAQ: COVID-19 Data and Surveillance | CDC
candidates.snippet: CDC receives line-level data primarily from state health departments. Information is de-identified and does not include names or home addresses. CDC makes line-level data available through patient-level data sets.

candidates.title: Preliminary U.S. COVID-19 Burden Estimates - Data.CDC.gov
candidates.snippet: This dataset represents preliminary weekly estimates of cumulative U.S. COVID-19 burden, including illnesses, outpatient visits, hospitalizations and deaths, since the start of 2024 respiratory season.

candidates.title: Data | Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidates.snippet: Data published by CDC public health programs to help save lives and protect people from health, safety, and security threats.
